title: Ordinary flat algebra and quotients of a completed constant ring
statement: Let T be a scheme, A a commutative Noetherian ring and I an ideal. Let B be the inverse limit of the constant ring sheaves A/I^(n+1), and let S be a specified isomorphic presentation of B. Let c: underline A → S have the canonical composites with every projection. Then S, restricted along c, is flat over underline A, and extension of scalars along c is exact. For every n, any ring-sheaf presentation H of underline(A/I^(n+1)) and the transported projection p:S → H, the scalar-extension morphism from the constant A-module A/I^(n+1) to H is invertible whenever it sends b tensor the constant x to p(b) times the specified image of x. All constants, tensor products and scalar extensions are the constructions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module] and [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; flatness is [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. This statement concerns modules in degree zero and asserts no complex, finite-projective resolution or constants-to-functions comparison.

proof.text: Replace the pro-etale site by AsSmall at the coefficient universe, using the topology induced by the equivalence. The constant-sheaf comparison is the inverse of the continuous-pushforward/sheafification compatibility isomorphism, and is normalized on the sheafification unit. Its naturality identifies the quotient systems. The preserved-limit isomorphism identifies their completions, projections and the coefficient map. Apply ConstantCompletion.flat_and_quotients in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] on this small site.

Use the proved explicit-site/monoidal tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] to express the existing flatness as exactness of the explicit tensor functor. The existing flatness yields local finite-relation factorizations by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-relations-universes]. Map each original relation through the constant and completed ring isomorphisms, apply that theorem on the small site, and pull the covering sieve back along the inverse site equivalence. Map the coefficients and sections back through the inverse ring isomorphisms. Naturality gives the original factorization and zero coefficient sums, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion-universes] proves flatness on the original site.

Interchange the factors of each sectionwise scalar tensor product to identify the underlying additive sheaf of scalar extension with tensoring by the restricted completed algebra. Pure tensors check naturality. Abelian sheafification gives the corresponding natural isomorphism after sheafification. The forgetful functor to additive sheaves preserves finite limits and colimits and reflects them: colimit preservation follows from the module-sheafification adjunction and its fully faithful right adjoint. Transport exactness of tensor by the flat module through this isomorphism and reflection.

Fix n and transport the surjectivity and generated-kernel formulas from ConstantCompletion.flat_and_quotients back through the completed and quotient ring isomorphisms. For X equal to scalar extension of the constant A-module A/I^(n+1), its natural section z=1 tensor 1 defines an S-linear map t:S→X. Balancedness and linearity of constant-module sheafification give t(c(a))=1 tensor the class of a, so t kills each generator a in I^(n+1). Induction on ideal-span membership shows ker(p) is contained in ker(t). Sectionwise quotient-linear-map descent therefore defines s:H→X with s(p(b))=t(b); surjectivity of p and naturality of t make these section maps a morphism of module sheaves. The assumed formula for r gives r(s(p(b)))=p(b). For the other inverse identity, use the scalar-tensor adjunction and constant-module sheafification adjunction; both maps agree on 1 tensor the constant class of every a in A, since s(r(1 tensor class(a)))=s(p(c(a)))=t(c(a)). Quotient surjectivity supplies every class and the two adjunctions prove s∘r=id. Thus r is an isomorphism. Empty objects, zero rings, I=0 and I=A require no extra hypotheses.

theorem completed_constant_algebra_flat_quotients
    (T : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (S : Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (e : adicLisseCompletedRing T I ≅ S) (c : adicLisseConstantRing T A ⟶ S)
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ e.inv ≫ limit.π (adicLisseRingSystem T I) (op n) =
      (constantSheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1))))) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite
      ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars ((adicLisseForget T).map c)).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit ((adicLisseForget T).obj S))) ∧
    exactFunctor _ _ (completedAdicChange T c) ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
      (d : adicLisseConstantRing T (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) ≅ H)
      (p : S ⟶ H)
      (_hp : p = e.inv ≫ limit.π (adicLisseRingSystem T I) (op n) ≫ d.hom)
      (r : (completedAdicChange T c).obj
        ((adicLisseConstantModules T A).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))) ⟶
          (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars ((adicLisseForget T).map p)).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit ((adicLisseForget T).obj H))),
      (∀ (U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ) (b : S.obj.obj U) (x : A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)),
        r.val.app U (tensorSection T c _ U b
          ((toSheafify (ProEt.topology T)
            ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj
              (AddCommGrpCat.of (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))))).app U x)) =
            p.hom.app U b * d.hom.hom.app U
              ((adicLisseConstantUnit T (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))).app U x)) → IsIso r
